memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Now the length of time the Israelite people lived in Egypt was 430 years. At
the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD's divisions left Egypt.
Because the LORD kept vigil that night to bring them out of Egypt, on this night
all the Israelites are to keep vigil to honor the LORD for the generations to
come." - Ex 12:40-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"To the very day." Not roughly. Not approximately. To the day.

Four hundred and thirty years is an enormous stretch of time. Think of how many
Israelites prayed and died without seeing an answer. Think of the mothers who
buried sons in the Nile years. From inside those centuries, it must have looked
as though God had lost track.

He had not. There was a date circled, and He kept it exactly.

Then comes a beautiful phrase: "the LORD kept vigil that night." A vigil is what
you keep when you stay awake watching over someone. God was not distant that
night, dispatching judgment from far off. He was watching over His people.
Psalm 121:4 says, "He who watches over Israel will neither slumber nor sleep."

And so Israel was to keep vigil in return, staying awake in gratitude for the
God who stayed awake for them.

If you are in a long wait, this verse is for you. God is not asleep, He has not
lost the calendar, and the day He has set will arrive exactly on time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How long have you been waiting, and what does "to the very day" say to you?
2. What does it mean that God keeps watch over you at night?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You keep perfect time and You never sleep. Thank You for watching over
me even in the long waiting. Amen.
